parsed.use_case: A data quality pipeline can scan a batch of signed measurements to find distinct three-record combinations whose values balance to zero, such as offsetting ledger adjustments or sensor readings. It must emit each value combination only once even when the input contains repeated values.
system_examples: Accounting reconciliation systems — identify three distinct adjustment entries whose signed amounts net to zero.
Scientific data analysis pipelines — find sets of three measurements whose signed deviations sum to zero.
parsed.explanation: Sorting followed by a two-pointer scan for each fixed first value takes O(n²) time after sorting, versus O(n³) for checking every triple; duplicate skipping ensures unique value combinations. This can make batch analysis practical for moderate-sized datasets, though the output itself can still be large; 3Sum is also primarily a teaching problem rather than a widely exposed production feature.
